content:
sasha_ops: Heads-up: spot GPU churn spiked in us-west this morning — ~30% of our spot nodes interrupted within 15m. Observed increased fallback-to-on-demand and higher tail latency for standard-tier customers. Anyone else seeing this?

deploy-bot: Alert: spot-instance-interruption detected in us-west-2 at 2024-04-01T09:20Z. 42 instances reclaimed. https://internal.alerts/spot/1742 :warning:

mike_infra: yep, saw it. Autoscaler started on-demand nodes but some request routes didn't switch cleanly -> backlog on batch/rerank queues.

kyla_sre: Gateway logs show a bunch of 504s while model containers were cold-starting/warming. We need faster fallback or hotter standby.

sasha_ops: Quick proposal: adopt a mixed-capacity pool pattern per region: 1) reserve a small baseline of on-demand GPUs for critical tiers, 2) allow spot burst capacity for standard, 3) maintain a tiny hot pool of quantized model variants on on-demand for instant fallback (hot-start). This minimizes warmup penalties. Thoughts?

lina_cost: Numbers: spot pricing ~0.35x on-demand on avg. But if interruption churn > ~20% the extra fallback/on-demand churn eats >50% of savings. Recommend a dynamic policy: if observed spot churn > 10% over 30m, shift standard-tier target ratio towards more on-demand.

ajay_prod: @mike_infra can we codify customer-tier routing rules? e.g., premium -> always on-demand; standard -> try spot -> fallback to quantized variant in region -> if insufficient capacity, region-failover -> final fallback on-demand in local region.

mike_infra: We can. Quick mock routing config (concept):
```
{
  "routing_policy": {
    "premium": ["on-demand"],
    "standard": [
      {"pool": "spot", "attempts": 1},
      {"pool": "hot_quantized_on_demand", "attempts": 1},
      {"action": "region_failover", "regions": ["us-west-2","us-east-1","eu-west-1"]},
      {"pool": "on-demand", "attempts": 1}
    ]
  },
  "churn_thresholds": {
    "roll_to_on_demand_pct": 10,
    "cooldown_minutes": 30
  }
}
```

kyla_sre: Also add an interruption handler on node preemption to: 1) mark node draining, 2) flush KV cache to redis snapshot, 3) move in-flight requests to hot pool. That reduces cold-start latency when we re-route.

sasha_ops: Action items: Mike -> implement routing config and canary in eu-west at 10% traffic; Kyla -> add KV checkpointing and test recovery latency; Lina -> run cost sims for churn scenarios (5/10/20/30% churn). Target: EOD for PRs/experiments.

mike_infra: ack. I'll open a PR with config and link a canary plan. Starting with eu-west 10% then scale.

ajay_prod: :thumbsup: I'll update the runbook and customer-tier docs so support knows expected behavior during reclaim events.

lina_cost: I'll run sims and post numbers here before EOD. If churn stays high we recommend temporarily raising on-demand baseline per-region.

sasha_ops: thanks all. If we see another reclaim wave, trigger the escalation playbook and @oncall.

mike_infra: FYI after digging: preemptions were concentrated on a single procurement pool (spot-az-42). We'll add diversification across AZs and instance types to reduce correlated churn.

kyla_sre: Good call. Also consider shorter KV checkpoint intervals (e.g., 30s) during high churn to bound warmup cost.

sasha_ops: Great. Keep updates short here. Will check back at 1700 UTC. :rocket:
